{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I picked the animal (a fish facing left, chosen because the tail fin reads from the outline alone) and drew the pad sketch in the first minute, so everyone could build from it. The fish was laid with about 97 dominoes, all connected to the start, and both tail fin tips were included. I don't know yet what the judge will say, so I can't claim the fish was recognised. I can say it was a clean, complete build with plenty of time left over.

**Execution:** I laid the top body line (stroke 1) and checked the fin area by inspection rather than by eye. When the lower fin bent off the upper fin instead of running straight down-right from the crossing, I called it and relaid it. That was the right fix for the shape, but I did it while Jack was about two-thirds done on that stroke, so I cost him some work and briefly crossed hands with Sofia. A quicker check on the stroke before I stepped in would have been better. After the check I held back from touching anything, since bumps were the main remaining risk.

**Collaboration:** I gave each person a stroke by name, and the four of us stayed mostly out of each other's way. The lower fin was the one overlap: Sofia and Jack were both heading for it, and I stepped in to sort that out. I thanked Jack and Sofia for their checks and listened to their reports on the crossing. Because our status reports to the manager largely repeated each other, I could have used that time to look for weak spots instead.

**Leadership:** I set the plan, assigned the roles and made the redo call in the first few minutes. I also decided when to stop building and keep our hands off for the last five minutes. My weakness is that I took over the fin rather than letting Jack finish and then checking his work. I would delegate that more lightly next time."}
